title: Canonical module and derived transport after forgetting the ambient base of an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Specialize the ambient-base extension of [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] to the unique $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Define its named absolute presheaf by $A_X(T)=\coprod_{s:T\to S}X(T,s)$, with restriction $(s,x)\mapsto(s\circ g,x|_g)$. Its identity and composition laws and fppf sheaf condition hold; its sheaf is algebraic. Denote this explicit space by $X_{\rm abs}$. For a map $f:X\to h_U$ to an $S$-scheme, its absolute map to the underlying $U$ sends $(s,x)$ to the underlying scheme map of $f(x)$. This formula is natural. The canonical functor from the small etale site of $X$ to that of $X_{\rm abs}$ retains the same schemes and scheme arrows; its chart map is the section $(T\to S,x_T)$. These maps are etale, satisfy the chart triangles and the functor is continuous. Restrict module sheaves along this functor with the identity on regular functions [def-trf-space-module-scheme-restriction] [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. This specified restriction is an equivalence. Denote its inverse by $A_X^{\rm mod}$; it is additive. Conjugating $A_X^{\rm mod}$ by the specified small-ringed-model equivalences [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model] defines the additive exact small-module equivalence $A_X^{\rm sm}$. Using the module derived categories of [def-sfb-space-derived-module-calculus] and localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], define $A_X^D$ as the functor induced by this exact functor on derived categories, for a common arbitrary localization morphism universe. No module, map, ring or space is chosen from a bare existence assertion: the presheaf and chart restriction have the displayed data; inverse equivalences are determined by those restriction functors.
